title: Relative clauses with a preposition: companies and economies

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with a preposition, such as *del que*, from B1 Unit 20 (*un servicio del que dependen muchas personas*, *el edificio en el que vivimos*). Put the preposition before *el que*, *la que*, *los que* or *las que*, matching the noun. Economic history needs them often: what a country depends on, what it sells, who gives it loans.

sections.title: Preposition + article + que
rows: el producto del que dependía la economía
the product that the economy depended on
los bancos con los que pagaban obras
the banks with which they paid for public works
los países ricos, a los que vendían materias primas
the rich countries, to which they sold raw materials
los países de los que compraban productos industriales
the countries from which they bought industrial products

items.spanish: El banano era el producto del que dependía la economía de varios países pequeños.
items.english: Bananas were the product on which the economy of several small countries depended.

items.spanish: Pedían préstamos a bancos con los que pagaban obras y deudas.
items.english: They asked banks for loans with which they paid for public works and debts.

items.spanish: Los países pobres vendían materias primas a los países ricos, de los que compraban productos industriales.
items.english: Poor countries sold raw materials to rich countries, from which they bought industrial goods.

items.spanish: La empresa de la que hablaban los economistas tenía plantaciones de banano.
items.english: The company the economists talked about had banana plantations.

sections.content: The article agrees with the noun you describe (*el producto del que*, *los países de los que*), and the preposition is the one the verb needs: *depender de*, *pagar con*, *vender a*. Never drop it: not *el producto que dependía*.
